subject: Peering flap causing retry amplification and timeouts - FinWave production
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@finwave.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finwave.com
Date: 2026-08-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - production (FinWave)

Hi team,

We started seeing a big uptick in 5xx and 429 responses to model requests hitting Redwood via our dedicated VPC peering. Impact started ~07:55 PDT — customer-facing flows are timing out and retrying, compounding the load. Latency to Redwood endpoints also jumped from ~40ms to ~600ms.

We've attached a short pcap of client->Redwood TCP flows (packet_capture_0802.pcap) and a few request IDs. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (deploys, config, peering maintenance)? This is affecting our payment flows, so high priority.

- Sara
Sara Lewis
CTO, FinWave
Attachments: packet_capture_0802.pcap (pcap)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sara.lewis@finwave.com; ops@finwave.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - production (FinWave)

Hi Sara / FinWave Ops — thanks for the heads up and the pcap.

Short answer: no service deploys from Redwood in that window and no config rollouts. We're treating this as a network-level incident (peering / NAT / firewall). I'm spinning up a triage channel now and pulling NAT/conntrack metrics for the customer peering path.

Immediate asks:
- Can FinWave share the client-side retry policy (backoff, max attempts)? If aggressive retries are in play, that will amplify failures.
- Marissa: please pull per-second 5xx/429 by route + connection-tracking counters for the peered subnet (both sides) and attach any recent host-level logs.
- Evelyn: can you loop in network on-call and advise whether we've seen peering flaps for the us-west-2 region?

I'll post updates here every 30 minutes until stable.

Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, sara.lewis@finwave.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - production (FinWave)

Quick triage update:
- Per-route 5xx/429 showed a sharp spike at 07:56 and sustained elevated error-rate for ~40 mins.
- Connection tracking on our egress NAT gateway for FinWave's peered CIDR is at ~98% ephemeral port utilization around the incident peak.
- I pulled the attached redwood-diagnostics-logs-20260820.tar.gz (contains short logs and NAT counters).

Hypothesis: transient peering route churn + high client retry rate => NAT ephemeral-port exhaustion on the peering egress path leading to connection failures and TCP resets. When connections reset, clients retry and create a retry storm.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Expand NAT ephemeral port pool / increase source port range on our egress NAT for FinWave (quick, but temporary).
2) Apply a short canary policy to route traffic away from the impacted peering POP to an alternate POP in the same region (we can fail back once stable).
3) Ask FinWave to temporarily reduce client-side retry aggressiveness (increase backoff).

Attaching logs and pcap. Will continue to watch metrics.

- Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-diagnostics-logs-20260820.tar.gz

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, sara.lewis@finwave.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - production (FinWave)

Looping in network and incident exec chain.

Network on-call confirms a brief BGP flap between our us-west-2 peering fabric and FinWave's transit (07:53-07:58) that coincides with the first error spike. That likely caused transient connection teardown on the peered path which, combined with FinWave's default retry window, produced a retry amplification effect.

Next steps:
- Network will expand the NAT ephemeral port allocation for the FinWave peering and clear conntrack entries older than 120s as an immediate relief (ETA 20 mins).
- We'll implement canary routing to an alternate egress for ~1 hour.
- Karthik / Sales: please prepare an exec note for FinWave leadership (we should include root cause, impact window, and short-term + long-term mitigations).
- Vivek: please prepare an offer for a more robust long-term configuration (dedicated NAT instance + explicit routing, and a proposal for a dedicated private egress appliance in their VPC).

I'll keep the execs updated; escalate to leadership if the error rate doesn't fall within the next 45 minutes.

Evelyn
Head of Reliability Operations, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sara.lewis@finwave.com, ops@finwave.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Action: temporary egress reroute + NAT pool expansion applied

Update for FinWave and internal teams:
- At 11:52 PDT we expanded the ephemeral port allocation on the egress NAT handling FinWave by increasing the source port range and cleared stale conntrack entries.
- At 11:59 PDT we applied a canary egress route that shifted ~20% of FinWave traffic to an alternate POP. Metrics show a ~70% reduction in 5xx/429s on the canary path and overall error-rate is now trending down.
- Attached are NAT counters and a short timeline in the diagnostics bundle.

Request for FinWave: please hold off full retry flooding for the next 2 hours while we monitor. If you can reduce retry max attempts from 5->2 and use exponential backoff, that will materially help.

I'll draft an exec note and include the timeline + remediation steps.
Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-diagnostics-logs-20260820.tar.gz

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: sara.lewis@finwave.com; karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Incident resolved: NAT exhaustion & peering flap - postmortem notes pending

Final status: stabilized at 15:45 PDT after full egress traffic reroute and NAT port pool increase. Error-rate returned to baseline (<0.2% 5xx) by 15:50 PDT.

Root cause (short): transient BGP/peering route churn caused connection resets on the peered path. That exposed a tight ephemeral port allocation on our egress NAT for the customer's peered CIDR. The combination produced widespread connection failures and retry amplification.

Short-term remediation performed:
- Expanded NAT ephemeral port range and cleared conntrack entries.
- Canary reroute to alternate POP while monitoring.
- Requested FinWave reduce retry aggressiveness temporarily.

Long-term remediation proposals:
1) Provision a dedicated NAT instance and explicit egress path for FinWave (recommended for high-throughput customers).
2) Implement automated conntrack pruning when ephemeral port utilization exceeds 85%.
3) Add peering flap detection to our routing runbook and auto-trigger a controlled canary reroute to avoid retry storms.

I'll publish a full postmortem and remediation ticket (INF-7890) by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone for the fast coordination.

- Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
